# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name

## Problem Statement

The new **Serial Seller** challenge (`ch-serial-seller`) must map to a persistent Steam achievement like the existing 12 challenges. The challenge-side mapping is added in the parent item (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J); this item covers the cross-repo pieces required before the parent can be reviewed.

## Users

- **Producers**: Need the Steam achievement registered on the Steamworks partner backend.
- **Developers**: Need the manifest entry to exist before the drift guard test will pass.
- **Players**: Need the Serial Seller achievement to appear in-game alongside the existing 12 achievements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains a `serial-seller` entry with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false`.
2. The Steamworks partner backend declares the matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` achievement API name.
3. The `core` submodule pointer in the main-street repo is bumped to the commit containing the manifest change.
4. The manifest drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) passes with the parent's mapping in place.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The manifest lives in the `core` git submodule (a separate repository: `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), requiring two repo operations.
- The `steamApiName` values must match exactly what is configured on the Steamworks partner backend, or Steam will silently drop the unlock.
- The achievement must not be hidden (`hidden: false`), consistent with the existing 12 challenges.
- The Steamworks backend configuration is a producer/external action that must be completed independently of code changes.

## Existing State

- 12 existing achievements in `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, all with the pattern `TCE_MAIN_STREET_<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>`.
- The manifest is validated by `validateAchievementManifest()` and the drift guard test.
- Precedent: MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC (bumping core submodule pointer).

## Desired Change

- Add one entry to the manifest for the Serial Seller achievement.
- Commit to the core repo and bump the submodule pointer in main-street.
- Coordinate with the producer to register the achievement on Steamworks.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — Add `serial-seller` entry
- `core/` (git submodule) — Commit the manifest change
- `.gitmodules` / submodule index — Bump the submodule pointer

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J**: Sell 3 businesses challenge (parent, blocked by this item)
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04**: Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (parent epic)
- **MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC**: Precedent for bumping core submodule pointer

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Steamworks backend delay**: If the producer has not yet registered the achievement on Steamworks, the achievement will not unlock for players even after code changes land. This is tracked as a separate action.
- **Scope creep**: Additional achievement metadata (e.g., icons, descriptions) may be desired later; record as a follow-up, not in scope for this item.
- **Submodule conflict**: Unlikely but possible if the core repo has concurrent changes; resolve by rebasing on latest core before bumping.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- This item was already sufficiently defined; no interview questions were asked. The description, scope, and acceptance criteria were clear and actionable.

## Dependency & audit resolution (2026-10-01)

Producer confirmed the Steamworks backend registration (AC2) is not yet done and requires a dependency chain. Two dependency items were created in the core project (CG store — the correct home for Steamworks backend work; worklog does not support cross-store dependency edges, so they are recorded here as cross-project references):

- **CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ** — Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine
- **CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1** — Register Main Street achievements on the Steamworks backend *(depends on CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ)*

**AC2 therefore remains unmet until CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1 completes.** This item carries the `do-not-delegate` tag while externally blocked so the downtime worker does not re-dispatch it.

**Merge state:** the item's work is integrated into `dev`/`origin/dev` as commit `dd11ea4` (core → `d2d1f322`). The stale feature branch (which referenced the superseded core commit `4a287d4`) was reset to `dd11ea4`.

**AC4 call:** the drift guard requires the parent challenge-side mapping from **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J** (which depends on this item, so no cycle is possible). AC4 is verified at parent integration time; the mapping is present uncommitted in the working tree today and will pass permanently once the parent lands.

# Intake brief: Port the Vite watcher-ignore (`server.watch.ignored`) guard to sibling game repos' `vite.config.ts`

## Problem statement

The core scaffold template (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA) emits `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` (covering `**/.worklog/**` and the dev-output trees), and `tce-main-street` and `tce-the-rising` already carry the block — but 8 sibling game repos' checked-in `vite.config.ts` still lack it: `AI_Hell`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go`. When any of these repos accumulates `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (AI_Hell already has 9 + a nested `ToneForge` checkout), the Vite/Vitest file watcher recursively walks them and exhausts the host `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` budget — `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached` — crashing the dev server and breaking test runs (the exact failure mode fixed in the parent item MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY).

## Users

- **Developers/agents working in any Tableau-Card-Engine game repo** (tce-\*) — must be able to run `npm run dev` and `npm test` from the main checkout once worktrees exist without tripping the host watcher limit.
  - *User story:* "As a developer in tce-blackjack, I want my dev server to ignore `.worklog/worktrees/**` so a recursive watch never exhausts inotify (ENOSPC)."
- **AI_Hell maintainers** (in scope — Q1 answered) — same failure mode is already active (9 worktree checkouts).
  - *User story:* "As an AI_Hell developer, I want the same watcher guard, so my `vite` dev server survives `.worklog/worktrees/**` growth."
- **Verification/audit tooling** — full-suite runs in sibling repos must not fail with ENOSPC.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Watcher guard present in every in-scope repo's checked-in config.** The 7 tce-\* repos each import `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin` and set `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` with the template's explanatory comment (wording as in CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA / `tce-the-rising`). AI_Hell (if in scope) sets `watch.ignored` from a locally defined constant covering `**/.worklog/**` (plus its dev-output trees). Verified per repo by grep of the checked-in file — no in-scope repo may lack the block.
2. **Per-repo regression guard test (mirrors the core/main-street ENOSPC guard).** Each tce-\* repo gains `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (copy of main-street's, minus the in-process dev-server smoke; static assertions only): the real config imports the shared list, spreads it into `server.watch.ignored`, and the list covers `**/.worklog/**` plus `**/data/**`, `**/tmp/**`, `**/results/**`, `**/dist/**`. AI_Hell gains `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` asserting its local list covers `.worklog`. Each test is picked up by that repo's existing test projects and passes.
3. **Surgical port only.** No other template drift is synced: no `resolvePagesBase`/`base` backfill, no blind re-scaffold (sibling configs predate those template additions), no local-config changes (e.g. AI_Hell's `configCsvPlugin`, `open: true`, port settings) altered. Per-repo `git diff` touches only `vite.config.ts` plus the new guard test; pre-existing unrelated working-tree changes (`.gitignore`, untracked `AGENTS.md`/`.githooks/`/`.worklog/plugins/`) are never swept into a commit.
4. **Suites pass and changes land on each repo's `dev`.** Each in-scope repo's own test suite passes (agent-initiated runs go through the test skill, per repo), and each repo's change is committed on its `dev` branch and pushed to origin, with commits referencing `MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0` (precedent: cross-repo item MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV). The pre-existing 1-ahead-unpushed local commit on each sibling `dev` is accounted for at push time (see Constraints). tce-main-street itself has no source changes, so its suite is unaffected; full project suite (each modified repo) must pass with the changes.
5. **Documentation reflects the guard.** Config comment matches the core template wording; where a repo documents `npm run dev` (README/dev docs — currently none of the in-scope repos has a README), a matching note about the `.worklog/**` exclusion. CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **No core/TCE repository edits and no submodule moves.** The core scaffold template and its guard tests are already correct (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA completed) and every sibling's pinned core commit (`09723c4b`) already exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` in `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` — verified.
- **Surgical only** — do **not** blind re-scaffold (`npm run scaffold` / `scaffold:games`): the current template additionally emits `resolvePagesBase`/production `base` behaviour that the sibling configs do not have; a re-scaffold would change more than the watch block. Port the `server.watch.ignored` block + import only.
- **Cross-repo working-tree isolation.** This item lives in tce-main-street's worklog but touches 8 sibling checkouts, all outside the tce-main-street worktree. Precedent MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV ("Cross-repo change ... # Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI)

## Problem statement

The single-player End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) gives the
player a deliberate review-and-advance moment after each turn. Competitive
(human-vs-AI) play has no equivalent: after the shared day's closing
presentation (`presentCompetitiveClosing`) the day auto-advances with only the
transient per-seat income text (`Player 1: +X coins | Player 2: +Y coins`, via
`perSeatClosingSummary`) and the incident reveal. There is no moment to compare
each seat's standing for the round just completed — businesses owned, income
and expenses per seat. This item extends the End of Turn summary dialog to
competitive mode: one panel per completed round (one shared day where every
seat finished and the closing ran), with **owner-keyed rows** (businesses
owned, income/expenses per seat).

## Users

- **Main Street competitive player (human seat)** — plays week-by-week against
  AI seats on the shared street; after each shared day's animations finish,
  wants a persistent panel showing every seat's round result and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action (parity with the single-player dialog).

**User stories:**

- As a competitive player, when the shared day's closing animations finish, I
  see one panel summarising the round with a row per seat (businesses owned,
  income, expenses, net change, closing coins/reputation/score) so I can
  compare standings and learn from the round.
- As a competitive player, I click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next shared
  day — the day does not advance until I do.
- As a competitive player, I see the same (disabled) **[ Bank Loan ]**
  affordance as the single-player dialog, so the loans option is planned and
  consistent across modes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score; the next shared day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**, and reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the single-player ledger; additions are optional and backwards-compatible — `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent.
3. The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours); **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.
4. Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the engine/headless close path; checkpoint save ordering (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged, and the dialog adds no save and mutates no state.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value (Phaser-free model tests for owner-keyed rows, engine per-seat ledger tests, and a competitive-mode browser dialog test); **all related documentation is updated** (docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md competitive closing and end-of-turn summary sections, plus any README/dev references); **the full project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked-by MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (outbound dependency): the parent item is
  still `open` (stage `intake_complete`) — its `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger
  does **not exist in the code yet**. This item builds on and consumes that
  ledger; implementers must land/coordinate with the parent first. Per-seat
  expense capture does not exist anywhere today — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  returns `void` and only logs — so the per-seat ledger extension is real
  engine work on top of the parent's ledger shape (kept optional and
  backwards-compatible throughout).
- Presentation-only contract: the dialog reads committed state / `result` and
  never mutates engine state or consumes RNG. In competitive, deltas are
  already applied to each `PlayerRecord` before the closing is presented, so
  the panel shows post-round values; the checkpoint save stays in
  `presentCompetitiveDayTail` (existing ordering).
- Overlay conventions (AGENTS.md UI best practices) exactly as the parent
  item constrains: `createOverlayBackground` + `createOverlayButton` from
  `@ui`; elements parented into `s.hudContainer`; depths 199 / 200 / 201;
  everything pushed into `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal; instant appearance
  (reduced-motion safe); button SFX via `safePlaySound`.
- Headless determinism and bounded pacing must not regress: Monte-Carlo /
  AI headless days (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`, `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`)
  never invoke the scene presentation and must never show/block on the dialog;
  the competitive closing bound (`COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`) stays.
- **Assumption (Q-scope, from repo evidence):** a "round" equals **one
  completed shared day** — all non-eliminated seats finished and the shared
  closing ran. The engine has no separate "round" concept beyond the shared
  day (`round-robin` seat iteration only), so "one panel per completed round"
  = one dialog per shared day.
- **Assumption (blocking safety):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one device
  (no networked multiplayer), so a blocking dialog gated on the single human
  seat cannot stall other humans. Interactive Q1 = A.
- The parent item's banking-hint ordering assumption is single-player-only and
  does not apply to the competitive panel (no banking-hint step exists in the
  competitive closing).
- `TurnResult` / `OwnerIncomeResult` additions must not break competitive
  callers (`MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing`,
  `perSeatClosingSummary`, scoreboard/HUD consumers) — keep ledger fields
  optional/absent-undefined-safe and guard with tests.

## Existing state

- `endCompetitiveTurnDay` (`src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`):
  ends the human's MarketPhase, drives AI seats to the shared closing, runs
  `runCompetitiveClosing`, then `presentCompetitiveDayTail` →
  station checkpoint save → `presentCompetitiveClosing(closing, () =>
  startTurnPhase())`. The new gate slots at the end of the closing
  presentation, before `startTurnPhase` (presentation path only).
- `TurnResult.playerIncome?: OwnerIncomeResult[]` **already exists**
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`): owner-keyed income, non-eliminated seats,
  in seat order, populated by `applyCompetitiveIncome`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, through `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases`
  in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`). Each entry carries
  `income.phaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown` (base / synergy / reputation /
  events / upcoming slots per owner).
- Per-seat ongoing costs are computed in `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) — staff salaries per owner, community +
  business running costs per slot owner via `ownerTaggedGrid` — but are
  **not surfaced** on any result (void, log-only). Businesses owned per seat
  are derivable from `ownerTaggedGrid` / `getSlotOwnerId`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`).
- Per-seat row conventions exist in `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`): `You` / `AI n` labels,
  `resolveSeatColour` seat colours, coin/rep/score columns — reused by the
  Game Over overlay model `MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`.
- Overlay precedent and single-player dialog model come from
  MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (its `MainStreetTurnSummary` model +
  `showTurnSummaryDialog`); docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md documents the
  competitive closing presentation (section "Competitive phase-major closing
  presentation …"), including the current auto-advance behaviour that this
  item changes.

## Desired change

1. Engine: capture and surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult` —
   per-owner ongoing expenses (staff / community / business), businesses
   owned, net coin change — extending the `OwnerIncomeResult` shape (or the
   parent's owner-keyed ledger) inside `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` /
   `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`; keep everything optional so
   single-player, N=1 and headless calls are untouched.
2. Model: extend the single-player Phaser-free `MainStreetTurnSummary` to
   render **owner-keyed competitive rows** (seat label + colour from the
   competitive scoreboard conventions) for the round just closed.
3. UI: extend the single-player `showTurnSummaryDialog(...)` (or a thin
   competitive sibling sharing the same panel) with **[ Next Turn ]**
   (primary) and a **disabled [ Bank Loan ]** button behind the shared wiring
   seam; gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` so the deferred
   (animations-enabled) path presents the dialog when the closing completes
   and only calls `startTurnPhase` after **[ Next Turn ]** — reduced-motion /
   replay / headless keep today's auto-advance.
4. Tests and docs: Phaser-free model tests, engine per-seat ledger tests, a
   competitive browser dialog test; update docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md
   (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections).

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` on the dialog (between closing-complete and `startTurnPhase`); presentation path only
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` / `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`: surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`: return/capture the per-owner expense breakdown (staff / community / business)
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — extend `TurnResult` (and/or `OwnerIncomeResult`) with the optional owner-keyed round ledger (expenses, businesses owned, net change)
- `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` / `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `OwnerIncomeResult` shape extension
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — extend the Phaser-free summary model to render owner-keyed competitive rows (reusing scoreboard label/colour conventions)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` + `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — dialog presentation + delegation (shared with the single-player panel); `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` per overlay conventions
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` — reuse `You` / `AI n` labels, `resolveSeatColour` colours for rows
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections)
- Tests: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` (pure model), `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` (engine), `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` (competitive overlay)

## Related work

### Automated related-work report (`find_related.py`)

- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary dialog (single-player seed)
  (open)
- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** – Bank Loans (open)

- Repository matches: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `core/AGENTS.md`,
  `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (keyword overlap: competitive,
  ledger, end-of-turn, dialog, seat, round, businesses).
- Duplicate check: `wl search "turn summary competitive"` returned only the
  parent, the deferred Bank Loans seam and End of game stats — **no
  overlapping completed item**; no duplicate/partial-overlap rewrite needed.

### Hand-curated context

- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — **parent / blocked-by**: single-player End of Turn
  summary dialog + `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger; this item's panel consumes
  that ledger and the parent's overlay/model. Not yet implemented (open,

- `MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG` — **Bank Loans**: the seam this item's disabled Bank

- `MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` — **End of game stats** (open, low): turn-by-turn

## Goal

Competitive play gains the same review-and-advance moment single-player already

# Improved activity log — filter by player / AI / all

## Problem statement

In competitive (human-vs-AI) play the Activity Log mixes the human seat's
actions, every AI seat's actions and shared turn/world events into one
undifferentiated stream, so a player cannot follow their own story or an
opponent's without reading every line. The log needs simple filter controls so
the player can view all activity, only their own activity, or only AI activity.

## Users

- **Competitive player** — wants to review what they did this game without
  wading through AI turns.
- **Competitive player** — wants to study an AI opponent's behaviour to learn
  from it.
- **Single-player / tutorial player** — must see an unchanged log; there is no
  AI seat to filter, so the controls must not appear.

Example user stories:

- As a competitive player, I want to show only my own activity so I can review
  my spending and income this game.
- As a competitive player, I want to show only AI activity so I can see how an
  opponent is building their street.
- As a competitive player, I want to return to the full log with one click so I
  can see the whole game in context.
- As a single-player player, I want the log to look and behave exactly as it
  does today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In competitive mode the Activity Log panel presents three mutually exclusive
  filter controls — **All** (default), **You**, **AI** — and the active control
  is visually distinguishable from the inactive controls by more than colour
  alone (fill/stroke/text treatment).
- Selecting a filter re-renders the log to show only entries matching that
  filter, **without** mutating `state.activityLog`, changing entry order, or
  altering the persisted save data. Filtering is presentation-only.
- **Attribution is complete enough for the filter to be truthful**: every
  entry created by an acting seat's action (purchase, sell, upgrade, event play,
  hire, loan, income, reputation, etc.) is attributed to that seat, so
  filtering by You/AI never silently drops or mislabels a seat action.
- Turn headers and shared/turn-level entries (per-turn net summary, incident,
  market refresh/deal-in, week start, game-over) remain visible under every
  filter so turn structure and shared world events are never lost. A filter
  with no matching entries shows a clear, non-blank empty-state line.
- The filter controls are hidden and the log renders unchanged in
  single-player and tutorial modes; the selected filter survives turn end and
  UI refresh within a session and resets to **All** on scene restart / new game
  (never persisted to save data).
- Automated tests cover the pure filter/attribution predicate and the browser
  rendering: each filter shows exactly the expected entries, attribution is
  asserted for every action path, an empty filter shows the empty-state line,
  and no entry is lost or duplicated.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (`docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`,
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only** — filtering must never mutate game state, consume RNG,
  or change transcript/replay output (`state.activityLog` is read-only during
  render).
- **Single-player and tutorial are byte-for-byte unchanged** — no controls, no
  attribution, no seat prefixes (existing precedent: `resolveLogSeatColour`,
  `getSeatDisplayLabel` no-op with no roster or one seat).
- **Preserve the existing Activity Log contracts**: deferred-render ordering
  (`logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`, MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2), scene-creation reset
  (MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6), auto-scroll/no-yank behaviour, word-wrap and the
  per-entry visibility optimisation.
- **Positioning follows the SLL layout authority** (`src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`); the `activityLog` zone is
  ~300 × 218 px with a 22 px title bar, so the control treatment must fit
  without clipping or hiding the newest entry.
- **Colour is never the sole carrier of meaning** — the active filter must be
  readable without colour perception (text/fill/stroke differences).
- Reuse the shared `createActionButton` helper from `@ui/Renderer`; no new core
  engine infrastructure.
- Keep the change surgical: per-seat filters, type filters (gain/loss),
  filter persistence and a Settings toggle are **out of scope** (record them as
  linked follow-ups if they come up).

## Existing state

- `MainStreetState.activityLog: LogEntry[]` — each entry has `turn`, `text`,
  `type` (`gain` | `loss` | `neutral` | `turn-header`) and, in competitive mode,
  optional `seatId` / `seatLabel` / `seatColour`
  (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`).
- `refreshLog()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`) renders **all**
  entries into `logContentContainer`, applies per-entry visibility, recomputes
  `logTotalContentH` / `logMaxScroll` and honours the deferral gate and
  auto-scroll.
- The panel is built once in `refreshStreet` (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`):
  `logContainer` → title bar (`'Activity Log'`, `LOG_TITLE_H = 22`) →
  `logContentContainer` → renderer-aware clip → wheel scroll.
- **Seat attribution is currently partial.** Only per-seat income/reputation
  entries use the seat overload `addLog(state, seatId, text, type)`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`). Most action entries (purchases, sells,
  upgrades, event plays, hires, loans) call the shared overload
  `addLog(state, text, type)` in `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`, etc., and
  therefore carry no `seatId`.
- Competitive mode is detected by the presence of `state.players` (absent in
  single-player); seat 0 controls the human (`controller === 'human'`, resolved
  by `findHumanSeatId`), every other seat is an AI (`AI 1`, `AI 2`, …).
- There is **no filter state** in the scene or the save shape today.

## Desired change

1. Add a presentation-only `logFilter` (`'all' | 'human' | 'ai'`) to the scene,
   defaulting to `'all'` and reset on scene creation.
2. Extend seat attribution so every entry produced by an acting seat's action
   carries that seat (`seatId` / `seatLabel` / `seatColour`); genuinely shared
   and turn-level entries stay unattributed.
3. Add three persistent filter controls to the Activity Log panel (compact row
   beneath the title bar), showing the active selection.
4. Filter the entry list in `refreshLog()` before rendering, recomputing content
   height and scroll bounds; keep shared/turn-level entries visible; show an
   empty-state line when a filter matches nothing.
5. Hide the controls (and render unchanged) when fewer than two seats exist
   (single-player / tutorial).
6. Cover the predicate, attribution and rendering with automated tests and
   update the docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — build the persistent filter
  controls inside the Activity Log panel (row under the title bar).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — filter entries in `refreshLog()`,
  recompute total content height/scroll bounds, empty-state line, ignore
  filtered-out entries in visibility and auto-scroll.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `logFilter` field (+ reset on scene
  creation) and any filter-control bookkeeping.
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` — shared seat-attribution helper / overload used
  by action paths; keep the prefix legibility contract.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `LogFilter` type and any attribution fields.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`, `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — stamp the acting
  seat on action entries.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — filter-row height / control constants
  (derived from the SLL panel width, not hard-coded panel coordinates).
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-filter.test.ts` — pure filter predicate and
  attribution coverage.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-filter.browser.test.ts` — rendering: each
  filter, empty state, single-player/tutorial unchanged, scroll bounds.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — Activity Log section: filtering and
  attribution.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — panel/control treatment notes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Attribution gap is the top risk.** If only per-seat income entries are
  attributed, a "You"/"AI" filter would hide most real actions and be
  misleading. Mitigation: extend attribution before shipping the filter, and
  test every action path (see Open Question 1).
- **Layout pressure.** The panel is 300 px wide with a 22 px title bar; a
  filter row reduces visible log height. Mitigation: derive the filter-row
  height from a constant and subtract it from `visibleH` so scroll bounds stay
  correct.
- **Deferred render interaction.** Filter changes made during end-of-turn
  deferral must apply on the next render, not force a render that violates the
  ordering contract.
- **Auto-scroll interaction.** A filter change alters max scroll; clamp the
  offset and preserve the player's "scrolled up" position, otherwise focus
  jumps unexpectedly.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Per-seat (AI 1 / AI 2) filtering, gain/loss type
  filters, persisting the filter across sessions and a Settings toggle are
  deliberately excluded; record them as linked follow-up work items rather than
  widening this item.
- **Assumption A (granularity).** "Player or AI ... all together" is
  interpreted as three buckets: **All / You / AI**, where "AI" groups every AI
  seat. Per-seat filtering is a separate future item.
- **Assumption B (persistence).** The selected filter lives in scene state
  only: it survives turns and UI refreshes, resets to **All** on scene
  restart / new game, and is not serialised into save data.
- **Assumption C (placement).** The controls are a compact row immediately
  beneath the existing title bar; the title text and title height are unchanged.
- **Assumption D.** The tutorial's existing highlight/hit-area expectations are
  preserved because the controls are hidden while the tutorial is active.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF** — Identify different AI players (completed): added the
  seat label/colour prefix to log entries (`resolveLogSeatColour`,
  `getSeatDisplayLabel`), the attribution foundation this filter builds on.
- **MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6** — Turn log no longer displays (completed): the log
  content regression and its scene-creation reset contract that must not
  regress.
- **MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2** — Activity Log should not show log line until the
  results have been shown in the UI (completed): the deferred-render ordering
  contract that filtering must respect.
- **MS-0MV1BMMO900824N9** — Restore Activity Log rendering (completed):
  `refreshLog` deferral gate and count-based re-render; filtering changes the
  re-render trigger, so this contract is in scope.
- **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** — Playable AI competitive mode (human vs AI)
  (completed): the mode in which the filter is visible and meaningful.
- Related docs: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (Activity Log section),
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (play-panel treatment and seat colours).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

### Q1 — Attribution completeness (OPEN QUESTION)

**Question:** Today only per-seat income/reputation entries carry a seat; most
play actions (purchases, sells, upgrades, event plays, hires, loans) are
unattributed. Should this item extend attribution so every acting-seat action
is stamped with that seat?

- (A) Yes — stamp the acting seat on all seat-action entries, then filter on
  complete attribution. *(Recommended)*
- (B) No — filter on the existing partial attribution only (accept that the
  filter will hide most player/AI actions).
- (C) Defer attribution to a separate blocking work item and land the filter
  afterwards.

**Recommended:** (A) — without complete attribution the filter is misleading and
would hide the very actions the player wants to review.

**Answer:** _OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer decision._

### Q2 — Shared / unattributed entries under a filter (OPEN QUESTION)

**Question:** What should happen to entries with no seat (turn headers, per-turn
net summary, incidents, market refresh, week start, game-over) when **You** or
**AI** is selected?

- (A) Always show them under every filter. *(Recommended)*
- (B) Hide them unless **All** is selected.
- (C) Show only turn headers and the per-turn net summary, hiding shared world
  events (incidents, market refresh).

**Recommended:** (A) — turn structure and shared world events affect every seat
and keep the filtered log readable.

**Answer:** _OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer decision._

### Q3 — Mode scope (OPEN QUESTION)

**Question:** Single-player has no AI seats and no seat attribution. Should the
filter controls appear only in competitive mode?

- (A) Competitive only — hide the controls in single-player and tutorial and
  render the log unchanged. *(Recommended)*
- (B) All modes — show the controls everywhere (in single-player "AI" would be
  empty or undefined).
- (C) Single-player + competitive, hide only in the tutorial.

**Recommended:** (A) — there is nothing to filter without AI seats, and
single-player visuals stay unchanged.

**Answer:** _OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer decision._

### Documented assumptions (non-blocking)

- **Assumption A (granularity)** — All / You / AI, with AI grouping every AI
  seat. Source: the item description ("player or ai, or ... all together").
- **Assumption B (persistence)** — session-only filter state; reset to All on
  scene restart / new game; not saved.
- **Assumption C (placement)** — compact filter row beneath the existing title
  bar, preserving the title text and height.
- **Assumption D (tutorial)** — controls hidden while the tutorial is active,
  preserving tutorial highlight/hit-area expectations.

### Research summary

- Read `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` (`LogEntry`, `PlayerRecord`,
  `findHumanSeatId`), `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` (seat overload and prefix
  legibility), `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` (`refreshLog`, deferral
  gate, scroll bounds), `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (panel
  construction) and `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` (SLL activityLog
  zone → 300 × 218).
- Audited every `addLog(` call site: 92 calls across 16 files; only
  `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` uses the seat overload for per-seat
  income/reputation. This is the evidence for the Q1 attribution gap.
- No filter state or filter UI exists in the scene, save shape or docs today;

# Engine DEVELOPER.md lists reduced motion among the paths that omit deferResourceApplication

Discovered from: MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X (Turn summary dialog suppressed by reduced motion setting).

## Problem

`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (the Tableau-Card-Engine submodule), section *Deferred End-of-Turn Mutation* → bullet *Deferred `processEndOfTurn`*, says:

> Tutorial, reduced-motion and replay paths omit the flag (legacy immediate behaviour, no regression — AC5).

After MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X the reduced-motion path does **not** omit the flag: the scene (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `endTurn`) takes the deferred closing path under reduced motion, so the Turn Summary dialog has a `requiresDeferredClosing` result to gate on. Only the tutorial and replay paths still omit it.

## Why it was not fixed in the MS session

- `core` is a git submodule (a separate repository, detached HEAD at the engine pin `5a16c2f`). A working-tree edit leaves the submodule dirty, and `npm run build` runs `engine:sync` (non-soft), which **refuses** to sync a dirty submodule ("never clobber") — every later build in this repo would fail.
- A local commit inside the submodule is discarded by the next `engine:sync` (it checks out the remote target), so the fix would silently vanish.
- The engine checkout has no worklog (`wl` there reports "not initialized"), and pushing to the engine repo's `dev` is not authorised from a game-repo session.

## Fix

In the Tableau-Card-Engine repository, amend that bullet so only the tutorial and replay paths are named as flag-omitting, and state that the reduced-motion path takes the deferred closing so a game's Turn Summary gate can present its summary dialog (cross-reference the game-side behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` no longer claims the reduced-motion path omits `deferResourceApplication`.
2. The bullet names the tutorial and replay paths as the immediate/flag-omitting ones and explains why the reduced-motion path is deferred.
3. No code change is required; the engine's documentation guards (if any) still pass.

Intake needs producer decisions before the brief can be finalised (stage left at `idea`; draft + Appendix recorded in the description).

**Q1 — Attribution completeness.** Today only per-seat income/reputation entries carry a seat; most play actions (purchases, sells, upgrades, event plays, hires, loans) are unattributed. Should this item extend attribution so every acting-seat action is stamped with that seat?
- (A) Yes — stamp the acting seat on all seat-action entries, then filter on complete attribution. **Recommended** — without it the filter hides most player/AI actions and is misleading.
- (B) No — filter on the existing partial attribution only.
- (C) Defer attribution to a separate blocking item and land the filter afterwards.

**Q2 — Shared / unattributed entries under a filter.** What should happen to entries with no seat (turn headers, per-turn net summary, incidents, market refresh, week start, game-over) when You or AI is selected?
- (A) Always show them under every filter. **Recommended** — keeps turn structure and shared world events.
- (B) Hide them unless All is selected.
- (C) Show only turn headers and the per-turn net summary, hiding shared world events.

**Q3 — Mode scope.** Single-player has no AI seats and no seat attribution. Should the controls appear only in competitive mode?
- (A) Competitive only — hidden in single-player and tutorial, log unchanged there. **Recommended**.
- (B) All modes.
- (C) Single-player + competitive, hidden only in the tutorial.

Documented non-blocking assumptions: All/You/AI granularity (AI groups all AI seats); session-only filter state reset to All on scene restart (not saved); compact filter row beneath the title bar; controls hidden while the tutorial is active.
